meta.title: The black-spatula calculation
meta.note: Paraphrased excerpt; the published correction fixed this number.

flags.detail: Recomputed 420,000 ng/d, but the paper says 42,000. Off by exactly ×10: a decimal or unit slip.

explanations: Typographical error: extra zero omitted or misplaced decimal point
Unit slip: using 700 ng/kg bw/day instead of 7000 ng/kg bw/day
Rounding or scaling convention: reporting value in µg/day after conversion (420,000 ng = 420 µg) and mistakenly wrote 42,000 ng
triage.check: Re‑calculate 60 kg × 7000 ng/kg bw/day, verify the units and any conversion factors applied, and confirm the intended reported value (e.g., ng/day vs µg/day).

review.impact: Yes, if the reference intake is actually 420,000 ng/day, the estimated utensil-derived intake of 34,700 ng/day would represent only ~8% of the reference dose rather than 83%, substantially weakening the claim that exposure 'approaches the reference dose.'
review.author_query: We noted that the reference intake calculation (60 kg × 7000 ng/kg bw/day) yields 420,000 ng/day, but the manuscript reports 42,000 ng/day. Could you please confirm which value is correct and whether the 83% comparison should be updated accordingly?
